html:
SMTO-BOOT-0017 — The environment name you gave the installer can't be used

GUID: 87c4ac35-ee53-42b7-bd42-58c0f4d4ab71
Slug: boot-conda-environment-name-invalid
Domain: BOOT · Subsystem: boot

What happened

  • The installer needs a simple name for the new Conda environment, the separate space where the model software goes. Your name uses characters it doesn't allow, or is reserved by Conda. Nothing was installed or changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Pick a name using only letters, numbers, underscores, dots or dashes, starting with a letter, number or underscore, for example vllm or my-vllm. The installer rejects spaces, slashes and other symbols so the name can't be mistaken for a folder path.
  2. Don't use base or root; choose any other name. Conda keeps those two names for its own main environment, so the installer refuses them to protect it.
  3. Run the installer again with the new name, for example ./src/vllm/install-vllm.sh my-vllm The name is the only thing to change; the installer stopped before doing anything else.

What success looks like

  • The installer moves on and prints "Using Conda" or "Installing Conda via Miniforge" instead of this message.

If it still fails

  • Copy the full terminal output, including the SMTO-BOOT-0017 line and the Error reference line, plus the exact command you ran, and send it to the person who manages your model setup. Don't keep retrying the same name; it will be rejected each time.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • install-vllm.sh rejected the Conda environment name because it does not match ^[a-zA-Z0-9_][a-zA-Z0-9_.-]*$ or is one of the reserved names base or root.

What this means

  • Conda environment-name validation rejects unsupported syntax or the reserved names base/root. Name validation stops before platform/GPU probing or Conda environment changes. A syntactically valid name may still refer to an existing environment; name validation does not query Conda.

Why this can happen

  • Conda environment-name validation rejects unsupported syntax or the reserved names base/root.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the name with allowed characters and the nonreserved-name requirement.

How to fix it

  • Pass a name matching ^[a-zA-Z0-9_][a-zA-Z0-9_.-]*$ other than base or root, for example ./src/vllm/install-vllm.sh my-vllm. This check runs before platform, GPU or Conda probing and does not query Conda, so a valid name can still be rejected later if that environment already exists.
  • Use letters, digits, underscores, dots or hyphens, beginning with a letter, digit or underscore. Choose a name other than base or root.

Retry and execution caution

  • Choose a name matching the allowed characters and not equal to base or root before running the installer again.

How to verify the fix

  • A valid distinct name is selected for the intended new environment.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Name validation stops before platform/GPU probing or Conda environment changes.
  • A syntactically valid name may still refer to an existing environment; name validation does not query Conda.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
